pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these crops has tiny seeds sown directly? (1 mark)
   A. Coconut
   B. Pawpaw tree
   C. Millet
   D. Avocado

2. Which item can be made with tacking stitches in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. A roof
   B. A car
   C. A handkerchief
   D. A house

3. What do body-building foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Make food taste sweet
   B. Only give heat
   C. Only quench thirst
   D. Help the body to grow and repair

4. Which cloth is easiest for beginners? (1 mark)
   A. Cotton
   B. Wire mesh
   C. Slippery silk
   D. Thick leather

5. When is even tacking most useful? (1 mark)
   A. For curves and slippery cloth
   B. When you do not want to sew
   C. Only for paper
   D. Only for straight seams that need no hold

6. Why does compost help the environment? (1 mark)
   A. It uses up all the water
   B. It creates more rubbish
   C. It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   D. It kills all soil animals

7. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Tell a teacher or an adult
   C. Keep using it
   D. Throw it in a river

8. Why is a damp cloth used for dusting? (1 mark)
   A. It scatters the dust
   B. It traps the dust
   C. It hides dust
   D. It dries the room

9. Which food is usually shallow fried? (1 mark)
   A. Boiled rice
   B. Eggs
   C. Tea
   D. Boiled maize

10. Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire? (1 mark)
   A. So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   B. To make the food colder
   C. To cook faster than a cooker
   D. To use more wood

11. How can a dustpan be improvised? (1 mark)
   A. Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   B. Use a sack
   C. Use a rope
   D. Use a chair

12. What might a hungry hare eat in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Metal
   B. Stones
   C. Young shoots of vegetables
   D. Glass

13. Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Soil
   B. Wet leaves
   C. Old CDs or shiny strips
   D. Mud

14. What is a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   B. A type of crop
   C. A tool for digging
   D. A bed for sleeping

15. Why should cleaning be done in an open place with drainage? (1 mark)
   A. To make noise
   B. To get wet
   C. To be seen
   D. So dirty water does not make a puddle

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Give three uses of tacking stitches. (3 marks)

17. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

18. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)

19. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

20. Give three times when you should wash your hands. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Millet
   Millet has tiny seeds that are sown where the crop stays.

2. C — A handkerchief
   A handkerchief is an easy first item.

3. D — Help the body to grow and repair
   They are rich in protein.

4. A — Cotton
   Cotton is easy to handle.

5. A — For curves and slippery cloth
   Even tacking holds firmly.

6. C — It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   It turns waste into useful manure.

7. B — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

8. B — It traps the dust
   Damp cloths hold dust.

9. B — Eggs
   Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

10. A — So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   Fuel is not wasted waiting.

11. A — Cut a jerrican or flat tin
   A cut jerrican forms a scoop.

12. C — Young shoots of vegetables
   Hares nibble young plants.

13. C — Old CDs or shiny strips
   Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

14. A — The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

15. D — So dirty water does not make a puddle
   Dirty water can breed mosquitoes.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before eating, after using the toilet, after playing outside, after touching animals, after coughing (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
